name: YAMAYA CORPORATION
court: inline advance court, main session 2026-08-03 (agent budget exhausted); generator was the mechanical EDINET shelf + FX overlay, so the generator-never-grades-itself invariant holds; no score reached 6 so no red team required
fx_context: USD/JPY 163.85 (Jul-23) -> 157.19 (Aug-2), +4.2% yen; IBKR IDEALPRO daily mid, tape-verified
verdict: WATCH 4/10 — the biggest FX leverage in the cohort attached to the worst business and the most locked register
mode_b_first: Independent read: this is a 2.2%-margin liquor and food retailer in Japan facing convenience stores and e-commerce, and the FY3/26 numbers say it is losing — recurring profit fell from JPY 5.57B to JPY 3.70B, down 34%, with FY3/27 guided FLAT. A retailer whose profit falls a third in one year and is then guided to no recovery is not a value stock at 0.60x book; it is a business in decline priced accordingly. The FX overlay is genuinely the largest in the cohort (imported wine, whisky, spirits are literally the cost of goods — at 2.2% margin and ~45% import content, a 4.2% yen move is worth roughly +65% to EBIT on paper) but a margin tailwind on a shrinking base does not fix a share-loss problem, and competitive retail passes input relief to the customer within a season.

mode_a_verification.register: Yamauchi family ~48.4% across two vehicles and three individuals + AEON 19.15% = ~68% LOCKED, free float <=30%
mode_a_verification.capital_return_negative: no buyback in 18 months; shareholder perk ABOLISHED 2025-05-15 — the opposite of the Cleanup evidence
mode_a_verification.tax_profile: cleanest on the entire shelf — 0.29 PFIC passive share on the FMV basis, the widest headroom examined

the_only_real_path: AEON consolidation. AEON already equity-accounts it with a board seat at 19.15%. Either they buy the rest or the 19% is a permanent ceiling — and nothing in the filings dates that decision, so it is an undated option, which the house does not pay for.

fx_leverage_estimate.CONFIDENCE: LOW on the import share AND on retention — competitive grocery/liquor retail historically passes input-cost relief through to price within 1-2 quarters. The pricing-basis test the AI-adopter screen taught us applies identically here: a cost saving is only worth owning if the industry structure lets you keep it. Liquor retail does not.

entry_plan.rationale: 0.48-0.51x book — the price at which the declining earnings are paid for and the AEON option is free; ~15-20% below spot
entry_plan.sizing: 0.25% MAXIMUM, and only in the band — an undated-consolidation case cannot carry a real position
entry_plan.note: the tax profile alone is not a reason to own it; it is a reason to PREFER it among names you already want

kill_triggers: FY3/27 recurring profit falls below the flat guide
AEON reduces below 19.15% or restates the affiliate relationship
gross margin fails to expand in H1 FY3/27 despite the yen surge — that is the pass-through test failing in real time
adjudication_spec: H1 FY3/27 (Nov-2026): does gross margin expand with the yen? If a 4.2% currency move on a 45%-imported cost base produces no visible gross-margin lift, the pass-through hypothesis is confirmed and the FX thesis is dead for the whole retail cohort — a finding worth more than the position.
